headline: Approved policy changes on district security, school bus cameras, and community use of school facilities, and rescinded policy EEAA.
summary: The committee discussed policy BGAA and agreed to research how other districts handle proposed changes. A public hearing was scheduled for policy ECAF on cameras on school buses. Special education policies and cell phone practices were also discussed.
decisions: Approved policy ECA District Security and moved it to the full board, 3-0.
Approved policy ECA-R District Security Procedures as amended and moved it to the full board, 3-0.
Approved policy ECAF Use of Cameras on School Buses, required the Superintendent to schedule a public hearing, and moved it to the full board, 3-0.
Rescinded policy EEAA Video and Audio Surveillance on School Property, 3-0.
Approved policy KF Community Use of School Facilities and moved it to the full board, 3-0.

POLICY COMMITTEE MEETING 
TUESDAY, JULY 14, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Policy Committee was held at NHS North on Tuesday, July 14, 2026.   
Ms. Raymond called the meeting to order at 6:02 pm.  
 
Present: Ms. Raymond, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Lamphier 
 
Also Present: Mr. O’Rourke and Dr. Andrade 
 
Also Present: Members of the Public, Channel 22 Videographer 
 
 
Policy BGAA - Policy Development, Adoption, and Review  
• Ms. Raymond reads the NHSBA update memo recommending the BDFA policy, which includes 
parental and staff input. 
• Mr. O'Rourke suggests adjusting the existing BGAA policy to include parental and staff input rather 
than adopting a new policy as Nashua’s existing policy is more comprehensive. 
• Mr. Johnson inquires about the process for including non-board members in the policy committee, and 
Ms. Raymond explains the legal requirements and past practices. 
• Dr. Andrade emphasizes the workshop model of meetings and the importance of inviting experts and 
community members as needed. 
• Ms. Lamphier proposes adding language to the policy that allows for community members to be invited 
on a case-by-case basis. 
• The committee agreed to research how other districts are handling the proposed BGAA/BDFA policy 
changes, including larger and smaller districts with similar demographics, and bring the findings back to 
a future policy meeting. 
 
Policy ECA - District Security 
• Ms. Raymond reviews the ECA policy on district security, noting changes and additions, including a 
new policy on recording devices. 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy ECA District Security and move to the full 
board.  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
 
Policy ECA-R - District Security 
• Ms. Raymond discusses the ECA-R policy on ID badges and visitor procedures, emphasizing the 
importance of consistent practices across all schools. 
• The committee approves ECA-R with the new section on visitors to other district facilities. 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy ECA-R District Security Procedures as 
amended and move to the full board.  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
 
Policy ECAF - Use of Cameras on School Buses 
• Ms. Raymond reviews the ECAF policy on the use of cameras on school busses, noting the addition of 
provisions from the Parental Bill of Rights. 
• The committee discusses the need for a public hearing before the first reading of the policy, as required 
by RSA 570A2K. 
• Dr. Andrade and Ms. Lamphier discuss the logistics of scheduling the public hearing and the importance 
of having legal expertise available for questions.
POLICY COMMITTEE MEETING  JULY 14, 2026 
 
2 
• The committee approves renaming the policy to "Surveillance and Other Audio or Video Recording by 
the District" and schedules a public hearing. 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve policy ECAF Use of Cameras on School Buses 
and requiring the Superintendent to schedule a public hearing and move to the full board.  Motion passes 3-
0. 
Policy EEAA – Video and Audio Surveillance on School Property 
• Ms. Raymond recommended rescinding policy EEAA as information is now in ECAF.  
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to rescind policy EEAA – Video and Audio Surveillance on 
School Property.  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Policy KF - Community Use of School Facilities 
• Mr. O'Rourke explains the financial changes in the KF policy, including a minimum rate of $40 per 
hour for facility use and additional costs for equipment. 
• Dr. Andrade discusses the need for trained crowd control and the importance of coordinating with the 
city for large events. 
• The committee approves the KF policy, noting the importance of fair rates and consistent practices for 
community use of school facilities. 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve policy KF- Community Use of School Facilities 
and move to the full board.  Motion passes 3-0. 
Future Policy Committee Plans and Special Education Policies 
• Ms. Raymond mentions the need to review special education policies and the creation of a parental 
advisory board by Dr. Vicente. 
• Ms. Lamphier suggests forming an ad hoc committee to discuss board goals and special education 
policies. 
• Ms. Raymond plans to provide a list of special education policies to the committee for review and 
potential updates. 
• The committee discusses the importance of involving the parental advisory board in the policy review 
process. 
Cell Phone Policy and Classroom Practices 
• Ms. Raymond raises concerns about the potential conflict between the current cell phone policy and the 
practice of using lock boxes in classrooms. 
• Dr. Andrade explains that the practice is more about classroom management than a policy change. 
• The committee discusses the need for student input and the importance of clear communication about 
changes in classroom practices. 
• Ms. Raymond emphasizes the need for any changes to be discussed publicly and in compliance with 
existing policies. 
 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to adjourn at 7:15 pm.  Motion passes 3-0.  
 
 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
